item.title: SiPHA’s trip to Gumine saves lives
item.description: Aerial view of Olegain Health Center in Gumine District (Supplied) A surprise health inspection by the Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) turned into a life-saving rescue yesterday after the team saved a pregnant mother who was about to give birth by the roadside in Gumine District of Simbu.
item.content:encoded:
Aerial view of Olegain Health Center in Gumine District (Supplied)

A surprise health inspection by the Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) turned into a life-saving rescue yesterday after the team saved a pregnant mother who was about to give birth by the roadside in Gumine District of Simbu.

The mother was found in active labour in the open bush during heavy rain, with no medical assistance and no transport.

The SiPHA team took her on board and rushed her to Gomgale Sub-Health Centre,in Kuman Bomai LLG where she safely delivered her baby.

SiPHA Chief Executive Officer Dr Kassi Ken led the Monitoring and Evaluation team on the trip from Dirima to Olegain Health Centre, a four-hour drive through rain and mud-choked tracks.

The visit was to inspect service delivery at Olegain, a remote facility bordering Kambia in Jiwaka Province and Karimui in Simbu.

Speaking to community members at Olegain, Dr Ken raised concerns over deteriorating road conditions and the theft of the facility's ambulance.

The ambulance, funded by the Gumine District Development Authority (DDA), was stolen and later recovered in Jiwaka Province. Police are investigating. Olegain Health Centre remains without emergency transport.

"Where people live, essential services must follow. Our health personnel cannot be expected to walk for days across rugged terrain just to collect basic medical consumables. When roads fail, healthcare fails and our people suffer." Dr Ken said.

Dr Ken urged community leaders to press their local representatives for immediate road rehabilitation, and said he would escalate the issue to provincial and national authorities.

The warning became real on the return journey, when the team encountered the pregnant mother by the roadside.

SiPHA drivers navigated the flooded, washed-out terrain, completing what is normally a three-hour drive to Gomgale in 40 minutes.

Had the team not been passing through at that time, the mother and her unborn child would have been left stranded without transport.

The incident highlights the daily challenges faced by mothers, patients and health workers in remote Simbu, where poor roads, stolen community assets and geographic isolation turn routine medical needs into a matter of life and death.

item.title: Massat: Ratification not the only way
item.description: Bougainville Vice President Ezekiel Masatt, has reminded Members of the House of Representative that the Ratification process currently underway in the National Parliament is not the only way for Bougainville to secure its independence. The Autonomous Bougainville Government has put forward to the National Government its final position mid this year, that it would transition into Self-Government b
item.content:encoded:
Bougainville Vice President Ezekiel Masatt, has reminded Members of the House of Representative that the Ratification process currently underway in the National Parliament is not the only way for Bougainville to secure its independence.

The Autonomous Bougainville Government has put forward to the National Government its final position mid this year, that it would transition into Self-Government by September 2027 and declare independence by 2030.

Since 2001, Bougainville has progressed the Bougainville Peace Agreement which will now culminate with the Ratification where the National Parliament is expected to endorse the aspirations of the people to be independent, expressed in the 2019 Referendum.

The ABG had since expressed that it prefers attaining independence through the Peace Process, where the choice of the people through the Referendum must be endorsed.

In their consultations, the National Government has recognized Bougainville’s wish, and the parties have jointly agreed on the Melanesian Agreement Framework which will guide the lawful and gradual transition of Bougainville into independence.

However, debate during various sessions of the National Parliament since the Referendum Result, the Joint Consultations Report and the Melanesian Agreement Framework have been tabled, have shown that the National Government might not be able to muster the three-quarters majority vote needed to endorse Bougainville’s independence aspiration.

Addressing a briefing of the House of Representatives by officials from the Department of Independence Mission Implementation during the last sitting, Vice President Ezekiel Masatt reminded Members that the Ratification Process under the Peace Agreement is not the only way to attain independence.

He’s pointed out two other ongoing options of using a Constitution to declare independence and lobbying international support.

Ezekiel Masatt says people must not have high expectations on the Ratification Process, but leaders must continue to work to prepare the region for independence according to the timeline put forward by the Autonomous Bougainville Government.

Mr Massat further stressed that the men, women and children of Bougainville will lead the independence agenda.

item.title: Marape urges Parliament not to rush Bougainville vote
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape says the Bougainville agenda must not be rushed. (Image: National Parliament) There is still mixed reaction on the floor of Parliament as the National Parliament continues its final debate on Bougainville’s independence agenda.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape says the Bougainville agenda must not be rushed. (Image: National Parliament)

There is still mixed reaction on the floor of Parliament as the National Parliament continues its final debate on Bougainville’s independence agenda.

There is still more debate calling for Bougainville to remain part of Papua New Guinea under a higher autonomy arrangement. Others have argued against recognising the result of the 2019 Referendum entirely, while some have thrown their support behind recognising the aspiration for independence and argued for a vote in support of Bougainville’s independence.

The Bougainville independence agenda is an agenda of the National Government, having been brought forward by Bougainville Affairs Minister Manasseh Makiba.

However, from the debates during the various sessions of Parliament, it has become clear that the Government may not muster the numbers to secure Parliament’s support for the result of the Referendum, the Joint Consultations Report and the Melanesian Framework Agreement, which were tabled in August by Minister Makiba.

Debates over the various sittings have shown that the ratification vote will be taken by Members voting as individuals, based on their personal conscience rather than along party or political lines.

More debate ensued today, with the House adjourning until tomorrow to continue deliberations.

Prime Minister James Marape told the House that there is no need to rush the debate to take the ratification vote.

He says that, with Papua New Guinea’s sovereignty at stake, there is no need to rush Parliament’s consideration of the matter.

Marape is urging every Member to have a say on the issue before the final ratification is decided during this critical sitting of the House.

item.title: Namah calls for caution in Bougainville ratification process
item.description: Tourism and Hospitality Minister Belden Namah speaking in Parliament during debate on Bougainville’s political future. (Image: National Parliament) Minister for Tourism and Hospitality Belden Namah has made his position clear on the Bougainville ratification process, saying the referendum result should not be confused with an automatic declaration of independence.
item.content:encoded:
Tourism and Hospitality Minister Belden Namah speaking in Parliament during debate on Bougainville’s political future. (Image: National Parliament)

Minister for Tourism and Hospitality Belden Namah has made his position clear on the Bougainville ratification process, saying the referendum result should not be confused with an automatic declaration of independence.

He said the result represents the political wishes of the people of Bougainville, but does not in itself grant independence.

Mr Namah also called on the Speaker to recognise the constitutional responsibility of Members of Parliament to remain loyal to the State.

He proposed that any Member of Parliament intending to vote in favour of Bougainville's separation should resign from their position.

Mr Namah also raised concerns about weapons disposal and questioned whether the Autonomous Bougainville Government [ABG] had been conducting itself in accordance with the required standards.

He acknowledged the suffering experienced by the people of Bougainville during the Sandline Crisis and paid tribute to the Resistance fighters.

Mr Namah proposed extending the existing traditional framework for the Autonomous Region of Bougainville by a further 20 years.

He also said readiness must be measured by results rather than simply the passage of time.

He urged Parliament not to reduce the constitutional process to a simple counting of votes while overlooking the safeguards needed to ensure a legitimate process.

item.title: Solar-powered rice mill boosts Nagamito farmers
item.description: Donated solar-powered rice mill at Nagamito Community (NBC News) Local rice farmers in the Nagamito community of Ungai Bena district, Eastern Highlands province, will now have access to rice processing facilities, enabling them to prepare their harvest for consumption and sale with funding support from CARE International.
item.content:encoded:
Donated solar-powered rice mill at Nagamito Community (NBC News)

Local rice farmers in the Nagamito community of Ungai Bena district, Eastern Highlands province, will now have access to rice processing facilities, enabling them to prepare their harvest for consumption and sale with funding support from CARE International.

CARE International recently donated a solar-powered rice mill and newly constructed storage shed, valued at more than K180,000, to the Hege Community Development Corporation, with funding support from the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and contributions from the Nagamito community.

The facility is equipped with 12 solar panels, an inverter and lighting to support its operations.

The facility will save Nagamito farmers the cost and burden of transporting their rice to the China Aid Juncao project site in Goroka town for milling, allowing them to process their produce within their community.

The initiative is part of CARE International’s Community Action Plans (CAPs), which empower communities to take ownership of projects that address their needs during disasters.

Nagamito women’s representative Angela Kafe said the project is a blessing for mothers, many of whom struggle to transport their rice to town for milling and sale.

She says the new rice mill and storage shed will ease their burden, save time and improve their livelihoods.

“Many of our mothers are not able to take our rice to town for milling and sale. CARE’s initiatives have changed our lives and therefore we are very grateful.

“This project will make our daily lives easier. CARE has looked after us, and the rice mill will greatly support mothers who struggle to process and sell their rice,” she said.

CARE International Humanitarian Project Manager, Emily Meren said that the project aims to strengthen food security and livelihoods.

She noted that CARE provided the initial support, while the community took ownership of the initiative by identifying it as a priority in its Community Action Plans (CAPs).

“You have proven that you can carry out the projects, the result of the work shows how much you have put in to get the result from your plans to address the need in Nagamito community,” Meren said.

Meren urged the community to take ownership of the operational plan and encouraged the project committee to raise funds for machinery maintenance and ensure the operation is maintained in the long term.

CARE International regards Nagamito as a model community for its rice milling initiative, with the project expected to serve as an example for other communities across Eastern Highlands Province.

item.title: Semoso calls for vote on Bougainville’s political future
item.description: North Bougainville MP Francesca Semoso makes her position clear in Parliament today, calling for the vote on Bougainville’s political future to proceed (Image: National Parliament) Member for North Bougainville, Francesca Semoso today called on members of Parliament to cast their votes on Bougainville's Political future.
item.content:encoded:
North Bougainville MP Francesca Semoso makes her position clear in Parliament today, calling for the vote on Bougainville’s political future to proceed (Image: National Parliament)

Member for North Bougainville, Francesca Semoso today called on members of Parliament to cast their votes on Bougainville's Political future.

She said November 24 was the date the Government chose for Parliamentarians to vote for the referendum result.

Semoso expressed her concern on why the vote for Bougainville's Political future has not taken place as promised by the Government.

According to her, Papua New Guinea will always be part of Bougainville's political journey and that the two governments will always support each other.

She further added that Bougainville will only move forward if the members of Parliament take this vote.

Semoso therefore called for this vote to take place and not to continue debating on the matter.

item.title: K3 million allocated for Bihute CS administration building
item.description: The board showing what the new administration building will look like. (NBC News) The Eastern Highlands Provincial Government has allocated K3 million towards the construction of a new two-storey administration building at Bihute Correctional Institution in Goroka.
item.content:encoded:
The board showing what the new administration building will look like. (NBC News)

The Eastern Highlands Provincial Government has allocated K3 million towards the construction of a new two-storey administration building at Bihute Correctional Institution in Goroka.

The funding commitment was formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] signed between the Provincial Government and the Correctional Service during the official groundbreaking ceremony.

Speaking at the gathering Eastern Highlands Governor Simon Sia said the new building marks a change in the Provincial Government's approach to supporting the Correctional Service through partnerships and targeted investment.

Governor Sia acknowledged that securing funding in the current economic climate is challenging, highlighting the Provincial Government's commitment to the K3 million project.

"This is an achievement and legacy we are giving to the province, and we are proud to see such change after so many years," Governor Sia said.

He said the existing administration building, which is more than 30 years old, has deteriorated over time and requires replacement to provide adequate working space for Correctional Service staff and support the continued operations of Bihute Correctional Institution.

Governor Sia said the existing administration building dates back to the colonial era, making the new facility important in providing Correctional Service officers with a better working environment to improve their services to communities.

Meanwhile, Correctional Service Commissioner Noel Sarei acknowledged the Eastern Highlands Provincial Government's support in addressing infrastructure and operational challenges facing correctional institutions.

He highlighted that Eastern Highlands is unique in having two Correctional Service institutions, Bundaira in Kainantu and Bihute in Goroka, reflecting the province's population and geographical size.

He said the partnership goes beyond infrastructure development, providing an opportunity for both institutions to work together to address broader social issues affecting the province.

"The MOU is not just about the building and infrastructure, but working together and addressing social issues in the province," he said.

Commissioner Sarei said the Correctional Service's priorities moving forward include rehabilitation, developing prison industries and supporting the reintegration of inmates into their communities.

He added that the partnership with the Provincial Government would strengthen Correctional Service operations and improve service delivery in Eastern Highlands.

Construction of the new administration building has commenced and is expected to take 15 to 20 months to complete.

item.title: Chan calls for New Ireland share in Simberi mine
item.description: New Ireland Governor, Byron Chan wants to see a 10% allocation split equally between the provincial government and the landowners. (National Parliament) Chinese Mining Company, Lingbao is a new 100 percent shareholder in the new Simberi mine, in New Ireland province.
item.content:encoded:
New Ireland Governor, Byron Chan wants to see a 10% allocation split equally between the provincial government and the landowners. (National Parliament)

Chinese Mining Company, Lingbao is a new 100 percent shareholder in the new Simberi mine, in New Ireland province.

New Irelanders through their Governor, Byron Chan are calling for a part in this share and an increase in royalties from the Lihir gold mine.

St Barbara Limited signed an agreement to sell its remaining interest in the New Simberi Gold Project to Chinese company, Lingbao Gold Group in September.

From this about K1.2 billion was to be paid in cash while K128 million was for construction capital.

New Ireland Governor Byron Chan says from this, a 20% acquisition of interest in the mine is being proposed by the Kumul Mining Holdings through its subsidiary, Eda Minerals Limited.

Chan is requesting that from this 20%, a 10% be allocated to the province, with half for the provincial government and the other for landowners.

He also called for the increase of royalties of 2% to 5% from the Lihir gold mine.

Mining Minister Solen Loifa in response says, negotiations for the 20% acquisition is before cabinet and decision once released, will be made known.

Loifa added that for the increase in royalties, negotiations by the state team are underway on the community development agreement and that Governor Chan can register this proposal during this time:

Lingbao bought St Barbara’s remaining interest in the New Simberi gold project for a total of about K1.35 billion, while retaining royalties over future production.
